name: Greek music theory (harmonics, rhythmics, notation, acoustics), Classical to Late Antique
overview: Answer to the user: yes, the sweep found many music treatises, but nearly all core Greek theory already exists in Russian. В. Г. Цыпин (Moscow Conservatory) translated Aristoxenus' Elementa harmonica (1997), Ptolemy plus Porphyry's complete Commentary (2013), the anthology «Музыкальные писатели античной Греции» (2019, 536 pp.: Ps.-Plutarch, Cleonides, Alypius, Anonymi Bellermann, Bacchius, Gaudentius, Nicomachus with Excerpta, Theon, Sectio canonis) and the first complete Aristides Quintilianus (2023). The Novosibirsk ΣΧΟΛΗ group (Щетников, Афонасин, Мякин) added Nicomachus (2008), Problemata XIX (2012), the fragments of Ptolemaïs, Didymus and Theophrastus (2012), the «Ptolemaei Musica» (2012) and Elementa rhythmica II (2015). English coverage is also good: Barker GMW I–II (1984/89), Mathiesen (Aristides 1983; Gaudentius in Strunk), Solomon (Ptolemy 2000), Pearson (rhythmics 1990), Jonker (Bryennios 1970). The real gaps are at the edges of the corpus: Philodemus' On Music IV (no Russian, no complete English), the music and organology sections of Pollux (no modern translation at all), the acoustics of Problemata XI (no Russian), the rhythmic testimonia in Psellus and P.Oxy. 2687, and Byzantine handbooks that pass on ancient theory (Pachymeres, untranslated in any language; Bryennios, English only; the Anonymous Quadrivium of 1008). The notated musical works themselves (DAGM) also have no complete Russian corpus. Recommendation: do not repeat Цыпин's work. Choose Philodemus as the flagship (hard papyrological text) and Pollux IV as a quick, feasible pilot.
already_translated_ru: Aristoxenus, Elementa harmonica (Цыпин 1997); Elementa rhythmica Book II (Афонасин 2015). Sectio canonis (Афонасин/Щетников 2015; Цыпин 2019). Cleonides (Иванов 1894; Цыпин 2014, 2019). Nicomachus, Enchiridion (Щетников 2008; Цыпин 2019) and Excerpta (Цыпин 2019). Gaudentius, Alypius, Bacchius, Anonymi Bellermann and Theon's music sections (Цыпин 2019; Theon also Афонасин 2009). Ptolemy, Harmonics, with Porphyry's complete Commentary, which includes the De audibilibus extract (Цыпин 2013). Aristides Quintilianus, complete (Цыпин 2023; II 1–5 earlier by Лямкина/Мякин 2012). Ps.-Plutarch, De musica (Цыпин/Лебедев 2017; again 2019). Problemata XIX (Щетников 2012). Fragments of Ptolemaïs, Didymus, Panaetius, Heraclides, Aelian and Theophrastus (Афонасин 2012). «Ptolemaei Musica» (Александрова/Мякин 2012). Sextus, Against the Musicians, is probably in Лосев's Sextus Empiricus (1976); not re-verified.

candidates.title: Περὶ μουσικῆς Δ' / On Music, Book IV / «О музыке», кн. IV (PHerc. 1497, with 411, 1578)
candidates.author: Philodemus of Gadara
candidates.genre: Epicurean polemical treatise on musical ethos, against Diogenes of Babylon
candidates.size: About 150 papyrus columns in Delattre 2007 (2 vols). Estimated 12–18k words, many lacunae.
candidates.edition: Standard: Delattre, CUF/Budé 2007 (copyrighted). Neubecker, Bibliopolis 1986. Kemke, Teubner 1884 (public domain, outdated): archive.org/details/philodemidemusic00phil
candidates.ru_evidence: No Russian translation found in RU or EN searches. Столяров 2022 (Филос. антропология 8.2) only summarizes Diogenes' views from it. SVF-based Diogenes fragments may appear in Столяров 2010 (ФРС III.2); not checked.
candidates.en_evidence: No complete English found; the OUP Philodemus Project has not published On Music. Passages appear in Barker 2001 (on Diogenes of Babylon) and in Woodward's UCL thesis on Diogenes (music and ethics).
candidates.other_translations: French: Delattre 2007 (CUF, complete). German: Neubecker 1986 (Bibliopolis, complete).
candidates.value: The only substantial surviving Hellenistic philosophical debate on music. It preserves the Stoic Diogenes of Babylon and echoes of Damon, Plato and the Peripatetics on ethos, education and emotion, and states the Epicurean case against ethos. Used by classicists, historians of philosophy and aesthetics, musicologists and papyrologists.
candidates.ai_feasibility: Low-medium: heavy lacunae and editorial supplements, so the translation must follow Delattre's text and apparatus closely. The argument is recoverable. No numbers or notation. Needs a papyrologist to review.
candidates.pilot_unit: About 10 consecutive well-preserved columns of PHerc. 1497 from the closing refutation, in Delattre's numbering with a concordance to Kemke.

verification.title: Philodemus of Gadara, On Music Book IV (Περὶ μουσικῆς Δ', PHerc. 1497 with 1578, 411 and other pieces)
verification.ru_found:
REFUTED: the sweep's RU 'none' is wrong. There is no complete Russian translation, but there are at least three published sets of Russian excerpts.
(1) А. А. Столяров, trans., «Диоген Вавилонский. Фрагменты сочинения О музыке (из одноименного трактата Филодема)», in: Фрагменты ранних стоиков, т. III, ч. 2 (Ученики и преемники Хрисиппа), Москва 2010, pp. 19–29. This is about 11 pages, almost certainly the SVF III Diogenes fragments (fr. 54–90) drawn from Philodemus' De musica, so it rests on the obsolete Kemke/von Arnim text. Confirmed from the bibliography of ΣΧΟΛΗ 6.1 (2012), https://classics.nsu.ru/schole/assets/files/schole-6-1.pdf. I did not see the volume itself; platona.net returned 403.
(2) А. Ф. Лосев, История античной эстетики, т. V (Ранний эллинизм), М. 1979, section «5. "О музыке" Филодема» (Philodemus chapter at pp. 245–268). It contains Losev's own translations of several passages cited by Kemke page and line, including one long continuous passage (Kemke 64,2–66,41) on music's lack of ethos. Seen directly at http://www.psylib.org.ua/books/lose005/txt19.htm.
(3) Е. В. Афонасин, «Теофраст о музыке», ΣΧΟΛΗ 6.1 (2012), pp. 111ff. It translates Theophrastus fr. 720 and 721A (FHS&G), taken from Philodemus, On Music '3.35' and '3.37' in Sedley's reconstruction. These are probably Kemke's 'Book III' columns, which Delattre reassigns to Book IV. Seen directly in the PDF above.
Not verified: whether Лосев (ed.), «Античная музыкальная эстетика» (1960) includes Philodemus. ΣΧΟΛΗ 6.1 cites it, but my search budget ran out before I could check its table of contents. Столяров 2022 (Филос. антропология 8.2) is a study, not a translation. Russian Wikipedia lists only Gasparov's translation of On Poems 5, not On Music.
Russian searches run: 'Филодем О музыке перевод'; 'Филодем Гадарский «О музыке» Диоген Вавилонский … перевод'; 'Столяров Фрагменты ранних стоиков III.2 Диоген Вавилонский О музыке'; '"Фрагменты сочинения О музыке" Диоген Вавилонский Столяров 2010'. I also checked the iphlib.ru entry «Диоген Вавилонский» and the raw text of the Russian Wikipedia article.
verification.en_found:
I found no complete English translation of On Music IV. SEP's Philodemus entry does not mention one, nor do Crossref listings or the Philodemus translation series (On Poems, Rhetoric, Anger, Death, Property Management). Scholarly English excerpts and paraphrases:
- L. P. Wilkinson, 'Philodemus on Ethos in Music', CQ 32 (1938), doi 10.1017/s0009838800025878
- W. D. Anderson, Ethos and Education in Greek Music (Harvard 1966), ch. V 'The Hibeh musical papyrus; Philodemus'
- A. Barker, 'Diogenes of Babylon and Hellenistic musical theory', in Auvray-Assayas & Delattre (eds.), Cicéron et Philodème (2001); reprinted in Barker, Psychomusicology and Other Ancient Musicological Writings (Peeters 2022), pp. 355–376
- D. Delattre, 'Vergil and Music, in Diogenes of Babylon and Philodemus', in Armstrong et al. (eds.), Vergil, Philodemus, and the Augustans (Texas 2004), pp. 245–264
- S. Halliwell, The Aesthetics of Mimesis (2002), ch. 8 'Music and the Limits of Mimesis: Aristotle versus Philodemus'
- L. Woodward, 'Diogenes of Babylon reading Plato on music', BICS (2011), plus her UCL thesis (not accessible)
I did not see the full text of any of these, so how much each translates is unconfirmed.
Barker's Greek Musical Writings I–II is not known to include Philodemus, and ΣΧΟΛΗ 6.1 points to Wilkinson, not Barker, for Philodemus. Bychkov & Sheppard, Greek and Roman Aesthetics (CUP 2010) does have a Philodemus chapter (pp. 109–116), but it translates On Poems 5, not On Music.
Online and non-scholarly: Latinum Institute Substack posts (latinum.substack.com/p/pherc-1497-philodemus-on-music-book and related pages) give English for a few columns (e.g. XXII–XXIV). They describe themselves as speculative and AI-assisted reconstructions and are unreliable.
To check: De Gruyter, Volume 4.1: The School of Chrysippus: Zeno of Tarsus and Diogenes of Babylon (ERC project, ed. Christian Vassallo, 30 Apr 2026, doi 10.1515/9783111427263). This is a new edition of the Diogenes fragments and should include the On Music testimonia. Whether it has an English translation could not be confirmed (the publisher's site returned 405). If it does, it would add a substantial English excerpt set.
English searches run: 'Philodemus On Music Book 4 English translation'; 'Philodemus "On Music IV" Delattre translation English Neubecker'. Crossref queries: 'Philodemus On Music translation'; 'Diogenes of Babylon music Philodemus'; 'Philodemus De musica IV'; 'Greek and Roman Aesthetics Bychkov Sheppard'. The WebSearch budget (200 calls) ran out after six searches; DuckDuckGo and Mojeek returned CAPTCHAs, so I used Crossref, archive.org and direct page fetches instead.

verification.source_text:
Public domain:
- J. Kemke, Philodemi De musica librorum quae exstant (Teubner 1884): https://archive.org/details/philodemidemusic00phil, also https://archive.org/details/philodemidemvsi00philgoog (flagged NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT) and https://archive.org/details/BSG_8XSUP76_145
- Editio princeps, Herculanensium Voluminum quae supersunt, tomus I, ed. C. M. Rosini (Naples 1793), with facsimile plates: https://archive.org/details/gri_33125008559995
Both are seriously out of date. Kemke split Book IV material across 'Books III and IV'. Delattre has since rebuilt the whole roll from PHerc. 1497, 1578, 411 and other pieces, with new column numbers marked by an asterisk. Several columns were also re-read with multispectral imaging.
Standard modern text: Delattre 2007 (CUF), copyrighted. Neubecker 1986, also copyrighted, covers only the PHerc. 1497 portion.
I found no openly licensed digital text of Delattre's reconstruction. A Neoscholia translation would have to use Kemke and Neubecker for the Greek while consulting Delattre, or get permission to use Delattre's text.
verification.recommendation: Still a strong candidate. No complete Russian or English translation exists, and the work is central to Hellenistic music aesthetics and to Diogenes of Babylon. However, the sweep's RU 'none' is wrong: Russian excerpts exist (Stolyarov 2010, about 11 pages of SVF Diogenes passages; Losev 1979; Afonasin 2012), so it should be framed as 'first complete RU/EN translation'. The main risk is the source text: the public-domain Greek is obsolete and the authoritative Delattre text is copyrighted. A sensible first unit is Philodemus' own refutation in PHerc. 1497 (Kemke 'Book IV', the Neubecker 1986 portion), e.g. the ethos-critique columns that Losev quotes (Kemke pp. 62–66). That avoids most overlap with Stolyarov's Diogenes block; Delattre's numbering should be keyed in throughout.

verification.title: Julius Pollux, Onomasticon IV §§56–111 (music, instruments, dance) / «Ономастикон» IV: музыка, инструменты, пляски
verification.ru_found:
This refutes the sweep's "none" for Russian. Е. В. Герцман has published Russian translations of Pollux's music passages in at least three places.
(1) Е. В. Герцман, «Древнеримский "Ономастикон", содержащий бытовавшие сведения об античной музыкальной цивилизации». М.: Квадривиум, 2022. 176 pp., ISBN 978-5-00207-110-4, print run 200. The whole monograph is about the music content of the Onomasticon. Sources: labirint.ru/books/942277/, bookvoed.ru, podpisnie.ru, slovo.net.ru/book/104865/. The publisher's annotation calls it a study of "the level of knowledge about ancient music" in the Onomasticon. Its table of contents was not available online, so it is unverified whether it translates all of IV 56–111 or selected passages.
(2) The Pskov regional library's profile of Герцман (pskovlib.ru/obzori/iskusstvo-i-nauka-vmeste-k-znaniyam/13481-evgenij-vladimirovich-gertsman) lists among his Russian translations "фрагменты из трактата Ὀνομαστικόν Поллукса".
(3) Герцман Е. «Инструментальный каталог Поллукса» // Из истории инструментальной музыкальной культуры. Л., 1988. This is cited in the bibliography of his 1995 book. The title shows a study of Pollux's instrument catalogue, very likely with translation; not seen directly.
(4) Е. В. Герцман, «Музыка Древней Греции и Рима». СПб.: Алетейя (Античная библиотека), 1995 (PDF: sno.pro1.ru/lib/gerzman/gerz.pdf). I downloaded and grepped it. It contains Russian translations of short excerpts from Pollux IV 55, 58, 62, 64, 66, 69–70, 73, 74–75 (a long passage on aulos types), 76, 79, 80, 83, 84 (Pythikos nomos), 88 and 104 (barullika dance), plus IV 185 and others. These are verified excerpts.
Not found: any separate full Russian translation of IV 56–111 published as a text. Ru.wikipedia (Юлий Поллукс; Ном) names no translation. It is unverified whether Лосев 1960 «Античная музыкальная эстетика» includes Pollux.
Searches run in Russian (4): Поллукс Ономастикон перевод музыка; Герцман Ономастикон Поллукса перевод 2022 Квадривиум; Герцман Поллукс Ономастикон статья перевод фрагментов; Герцман Поллукс авлос Ономастикона IV перевод.

If the project goes ahead, start with the instrument catalogue (about IV 57–90: string, wind and percussion instruments, aulos types, salpinx), framed as the first complete annotated English translation and a new Russian one that engages with Герцман.

verification.title: Ps.-Aristotle, Problemata XI (Hosa peri phōnēs / "On the Voice"; acoustics, c. Bekker 898b–906a, about 62 problems)
verification.ru_found: I found no Russian translation of Book XI, whole or partial. (1) Orlov's list of Russian Aristotle translations (journals.rcsi.science/2713-3125/article/view/305639, fetched) names only three Problemata books: XV (Щетников, ΣΧΟΛΗ 13.2, 2019, pp. 521–527), XIX (Щетников, ΣΧΟΛΗ 6.1, 2012, pp. 87–97; first published in «Пифагорейская гармония», 2005) and XXX (Россиус, «Мера вещей», 2015, pp. 582–595). Book XI is not on it. (2) I extracted the full text of ΣΧΟΛΗ 6.1 (classics.nsu.ru/schole/assets/files/schole-6-1.pdf). Щетников's XIX preface says nothing about XI. Афонасин's notes to Theophrastus' musical fragments in the same issue (around pp. 119–125) only point to XI.6, 13, 15, 16, 19, 20, 21 and 23. One footnote renders a single clause of XI.6 in Russian ("как звук от упавшего тела распространяется во всех направлениях"). That is a passing quotation, not a translation. (3) Позднев, «Психология искусства. Учение Аристотеля» (aristotle.rhga.ru PDF, full-text index checked): the Problemata citations come from Books I, VII, XIX, XXVIII and XXX, none from XI. (4) Бержинская, «Пение как природный процесс. Понимание голоса в трудах Аристотеля» (cyberleninka, 2010) quotes De anima, GA, De sensu, Poetics and Rhetoric, not Problemata XI. (5) Web searches in Russian ("Проблемы XI о голосе перевод", "Псевдо-Аристотель Проблемы книга XI перевод", "Щетников Проблемы XI ΣΧΟΛΗ", "Проблемы почему голос перевод") found nothing. Caveat: I could not check the table of contents of Лосев–Шестаков, «Античная музыкальная эстетика» (1960), or Лосев's ИАЭ IV for stray excerpts from XI. The session ran out of web searches after 3 Russian and 2 English queries, and no online copy could be fetched directly.

It was published in 1927, so it is very likely public domain in the US. The revised version is in Barnes, Complete Works of Aristotle, vol. 2 (Princeton 1984). (2) W. S. Copyright: the Greek text of a medieval work is not itself protected. EU law limits protection of critical editions of public-domain works to at most 30 years (Directive 2006/116/EC, art. 5), and Italy to 20, so the constituted text is very likely free to use. Stéphanou's apparatus and Tannery's or Stéphanou's French prose should not be reproduced wholesale; legal review advised. TLG also contains the Tannery text (subscription only).
verification.recommendation: This is a good candidate: as far as I could verify there is no Russian or English translation, and the only modern-language work on it is Vincent's 1847 French chapter summaries. The text is a substantial Byzantine compilation from Ptolemy, Nicomachus, Aristoxenus and Archytas, and the main source of Bryennios. Expect lower novelty in the passages that paraphrase Ptolemy, since Ptolemy's Harmonics is already translated (Barker, Solomon). Start with chs. 1–15 (consonances and ratios through the genera of Archytas, Aristoxenus and Ptolemy). The standard edition, Pöhlmann & West, Documents of Ancient Greek Music (Oxford 2001; 61 items, 23 of them new since 1970), gives the Greek text, notation, transcription and commentary but deliberately no translations. The World History Encyclopedia review notes "the absence of translations of the Greek" (worldhistory.org/review/112). Translations of individual pieces are scattered:
- J. G. Landels, Music in Ancient Greece and Rome (1999): sections of both Delphic hymns, Mesomedes and Seikilos (cited in en.wikipedia "Delphic Hymns" and "Seikilos epitaph").
- A. d'Angour: first verse of the First Delphic Hymn in Brown & d'Angour 2017; the Seikilos distich in 2021.
- Rohland 2022: Seikilos.
- C. H. Cosgrove, An Ancient Christian Hymn with Musical Notation: P.Oxy. 1786 (2011): full text, translation and commentary of the Oxyrhynchus hymn; Wikipedia also cites it for Mesomedes.
- Grenfell & Hunt, P.Oxy. XV (1922): editio princeps of the Oxyrhynchus hymn.
- Wikipedia articles carry translations of Seikilos, the Oxyrhynchus hymn and parts of the Delphic hymns.
Not verified: M. L. West, Ancient Greek Music (1992, ch. 10) and T. Mathiesen, Apollo's Lyre (1999) probably translate some items, and Furley & Bremer, Greek Hymns (2001) may include the Delphic paeans; I could not open their tables of contents. Barker's Greek Musical Writings I–II and Strunk's Source Readings are collections of treatises and literary testimony, not of the notated documents.
Note: the WebSearch budget ran out (200 per session) after 1 English WebSearch, so the English checks were done by fetching pages directly (Wikipedia, BMCR, World History Encyclopedia, Open Library, archive.org) instead of the 4 searches requested.

Pöhlmann, Denkmäler altgriechischer Musik (1970) is an edition; whether it translates is not verified. The Hymn to Nemesis was translated into German three times in the 18th century, by Chr. Stolberg (1782), Herder (1786) and J. F. Degen (1787), according to Грабарь-Пассек's introduction on simposium.ru. de.wikipedia "Delphische Hymnen" has a partial German translation, unattributed.

Spanish: none found; es.wikipedia "Himnos délficos" has no translation.
verification.source_text:
Public-domain sources:
- Karl von Jan, Musici Scriptores Graeci (Teubner, 1895): includes "melodiarum veterum quidquid exstat" (Seikilos, Mesomedes and others). archive.org: musiciscriptoresjank, musiciscriptores01jank.
- Jan, Musici Scriptores Graeci, Supplementum: Melodiarum reliquiae (Teubner, 1899), which adds the Delphic hymns. archive.org: musiciscriptores00jank, musiciscriptoresjanksupp.
- Crusius, Die delphischen Hymnen (1894), archive.org diedelphischenhy00crusuoft.
- Weil and Reinach in BCH 1893–94 (Persée).
- Grenfell & Hunt, P.Oxy. XV (1922) for the Oxyrhynchus hymn.
The Jan volumes predate the papyrus finds (Oxyrhynchus, Berlin, Vienna, Michigan, Leiden and others), so for those items, and for current readings of the Delphic hymns, the authority is Pöhlmann & West 2001 (copyrighted) and Bélis 1992 (copyrighted). The ancient Greek texts themselves are public domain, so a working text can be built from Jan 1899, Grenfell & Hunt 1922 and Weil 1893–94, then checked against DAGM.
verification.recommendation: The famous pieces (Seikilos, Mesomedes' Hymns to Nemesis and to Helios, the Oxyrhynchus hymn, the Euripides papyri) are already translated in Russian and English, so the corpus is not untranslated as a whole. Two real gaps remain. First, I found no Russian translation of the two Delphic paeans (Athenaios c. 138 BCE, Limenios 128 BCE), so they are the best first unit: a first Russian (plus English) annotated translation with notation-aware commentary. Second, no Russian or English translation covers the whole corpus (DAGM's 61 items); a complete annotated corpus, including the small papyrus fragments, would be new in both languages.

name: Latin, Byzantine-ecclesiastical and Oriental (Syriac/Arabic/Armenian) music-theoretical writing transmitting ancient theory
overview:
Yes, the finds include music texts: 8 treatises across Latin, Byzantine church and Arabic writing. Russian coverage of this corpus's core Latin texts is now much better than the starting list assumed. Full Russian translations exist for:
- Boethius (Лебедев 2012)
- Augustine, De musica (Двоскина 2017)
- Martianus Capella, all books including IX (Шахов 2019)
- Macrobius' Commentary together with Favonius Eulogius (Звиревич 2024)
- Isidore, Etymologies I–III
- Censorinus, De die natali (ВДИ 1986)
- Cassiodorus, Institutiones II.5 (Бродская 1991)
- Niceta of Remesiana (2018)

So Favonius and Macrobius II.1–4 drop out as candidates. The real gaps are:
- Calcidius' harmonic chapters. Only his chapters on demons exist in Russian (Гараджа 2023).
- The Pseudo-Censorinus Fragmentum, a short Latin epitome covering music, rhythm and metre. Only an unpublished student version of chs. X–XII exists (МГК «Musica theorica», 1995–2012). The same collection also holds other unpublished Carolingian fragments.
- Byzantine church-chant theory. Герцман wrote studies and published the «Петербургский теоретикон» (1994); otherwise nothing in Russian.
- Arabic music theory. Only excerpts exist, e.g. al-Kindi in Нофал 2017.

In English, Calcidius (Magee 2016), De audibilibus (Barker, GMW II, 1989, ch. 5; Loeb 1936) and the Hagiopolites (Raasted 1983) are covered. Byzantine treatises are mostly in German (Wolfram/Hannick, Wien), al-Kindi in German (Lachmann–El-Hefni 1931; Schewe 2018, 2025), and the Censorinus Fragment in Spanish (Gredos BCG 372). I found no pre-1300 Syriac or Armenian music treatise worth translating. Remaining gaps were not verified because the web-search budget ran out mid-task.

Its bibliography lists no earlier Russian translation. For a general overview it cites only Лосев 1992 (ИАЭ т. 8.1, «Итоги тысячелетнего развития», гл. II «Продолжатели (Халкидий и Макробий)», §1 «Халкидий», incl. «Содержание комментария Халкидия»). That is a survey, not a translation. It may contain Losev's own paraphrases or short quotations of the world-soul and harmonic sections, but I could not check its text. Russian Wikipedia «Халкидий» also lists no Russian translation; its literature section has Петрова М. С., «Калкидий», in «Античная философия: энциклопедический словарь» (2008, 403–407), Лосев ИАЭ VIII, and Диллон, «Средние платоники». Six Russian searches found nothing for chs. 32–55: «Халкидий Комментарий к Тимею перевод»; «Халкидий гармония музыка Тимей перевод фрагмент»; «Халкидий перевод с латинского … Платоновские исследования»; «Халкидий о судьбе/о материи/о душе перевод»; «Гараджа Халкидий»; «Халкидий мировая душа гармония пифагорейцы числа». The search budget ran out before I could check Лосев–Шестаков 1960, Шестаков 1966 or Герцман's monographs directly for quoted passages, so those remain unverified. verification.source_text: The best open digital text is the Thesaurus Musicarum Latinarum file CHALTIM. It is J. Wrobel's edition (Leipzig: Teubner 1876; Minerva reprint 1963), which is public domain, digitized for TML in 2005 by L. Vest, D. Schneider and T. J. Mathiesen. It contains Calcidius' whole Timaeus translation and the complete commentary to ch. CCCLV, with the descriptiones (diagrams VII–IX for the harmonic chapters) as TML figure files. The original URL is www.chmtl.indiana.edu/tml/3rd-5th/CHALTIM, which currently redirects because of an Indiana outage. Provisional mirror: https://lightseagreen-dog-349934.hostingersite.com/tml/3rd-5th/CHALTIM. I checked it: chs. XXXII–LV, with the headings DE ORTU ANIMAE, DE MODULATIONE SIUE HARMONIA and DE NUMERIS, come to about 5,800 Latin words. Print scans: the 1520 Paris editio princeps is public domain on archive.org (ids chalcidijlucule00unkngoog, bub_gb_t-tyWOP6VRYC, bub_gb_LxGcsxR3tWgC). I found no archive.org scan of Wrobel 1876; there is a HathiTrust record 100245248, but its access status was not checked (403). The standard critical text is Waszink, Plato Latinus IV (Warburg/Brill 1962, 2nd ed. 1975), which is still under copyright; a scan circulates on archive.org (makhankov_gmail_0002_201505). Use it and Bakhouche 2011 and Magee 2016 for collation only.
verification.recommendation: This is a Russian-only gap. Complete EN, IT, FR and ES translations exist, so it fails priority 2 and ranks below untranslated texts, but it suits a Russian-first Neoscholia unit: it is the key Latin channel of Adrastus/Theon harmonics into the medieval West, and a short, public-domain text (Wrobel/TML) is available. Start with chs. 40–45 (De modulatione sive harmonia) and extend to the full block 32–55 (about 5,800 words, with diagrams). Before publishing, check Losev ИАЭ VIII.1 §1 for any quoted passages.

verification.ru_found:
I found one Russian translation, and it was never formally published. In the Moscow Conservatory's own catalogue of the Musica theorica collections (mosconsv.ru/upload/images/Documents/Events/musica-theorica-catalog.pdf), the section «Гармонические древности» lists, for vol. V: «Цензорин Х [?]. Фрагменты «Фрагментов» (главы X–XII) (Перевод М. Переверзевой, редакция Р. Л. Поспеловой)», p. 10. Vol. V is Musica theorica-5 (compiled by Ю. Н. Холопов, edited by В. С. Ценова, МГК, 1999). It is marked «на правах рукописи», and the catalogue says the volumes are kept only in the Conservatory reading room. The same volume has an essay by М. Переверзева, «Из греков — в ромеи. Цензорин и его „Книга о дне рождения“» (p. 7). Chapters X–XII cover de nomine rhythmi, de musica and de modulatione; ch. 9 and the metre chapters 13–15 are not included. So this is an unpublished partial translation, as the sweep said.
The full Russian translation of De die natali by В. Л. Цымбурский (ВДИ 1986, nos. 2–3) does not include the fragment. I checked the PDF of the second part (vdi.igh.ru, VDI 1986 no. 3, pp. 224–237): it ends with DDN 24, and the translator's last note says the text breaks off there. It contains no Fragmentum material.
Searches run: «Цензорин фрагмент перевод "О музыке" метры» and «Цензорин "О дне рождения" перевод фрагмент музыка ритм» (no relevant hits apart from the MGK catalogue), «Цензорин "Книга о дне рождения" перевод» (found only Цымбурский), and «"Античная музыкальная эстетика" Цензорин». The Лосев 1960 anthology cites only De die natali ch. 12 (music therapy); I found nothing showing it uses the Fragmentum. A CyberLeninka API query returned 0 hits, which may be an API fault. My WebSearch budget ran out after 4 searches (2 Russian, 2 English), so I could not run the required 4+4. The remaining checks were direct catalogue and file fetches.
verification.en_found:
The sweep's 'unknown' is wrong: a complete English translation exists. L. K. M. Maisel, 'The Fragmentum Censorini, also known as the Epitoma disciplinarum', version 1.03 dated 15.02.2020, translated from Sallmann's 1983 Teubner text with footnotes. It is on the Internet Archive at https://archive.org/details/fragmentumcensorini (PDF and text, 17 pp.) under a Public Domain Mark 1.0.
I downloaded the full text and checked it. It covers all of chs. 1–15, including '9. On Music', '10. On the Word Rhythm', '11. On Music', '12. On the Modes' (de modulatione), '13. On Meters, i.e. Numeri', '14. On the Established Meters' and '15. On Simple Meters'. The music sections are complete as far as the lacunose text allows, with notes comparing Martianus Capella and Aristides Quintilianus and citing Barker's GMW II.
Parker's 2007 Chicago translation covers De die natali only. Barker's GMW I–II contain only Greek texts and do not include this fragment. I was not able to check Mathiesen or Strunk.

verification.title: [Ps.-Aristotle], De audibilibus / Περὶ ἀκουστῶν / «О слышимом» (Bekker 800a1–804b39 = Porphyry, In Ptol. Harm. 67.24–77.18 Düring), with Problemata XI as a companion unit
verification.ru_found:
This refutes the sweep's RU "partial" verdict. A complete Russian translation exists, but it sits inside Porphyry's commentary, which is why the bibliographies missed it.
(1) FULL: Клавдий Птолемей. Гармоника в трёх книгах; Порфирий. Комментарий к «Гармонике» Птолемея. Издание подготовил В. Г. Цыпин. М.: НИЦ «Московская консерватория», 2013, 456 pp. (ISBN 978-5-89598-288-4; publisher page https://www.mosconsv.ru/ru/publication/134660). The publisher's annotation says Porphyry's Commentary is translated, and that this was the first translation into any modern European language. I checked the OCR full text on archive.org (https://archive.org/details/2013_20210528). Porphyry introduces the quotation with «Занимаясь различиями голосов в книге «О слышимом», он, в частности, говорит…» on about p. 79. The quotation runs through about p. 88, with Düring page numbers 67–77/78 in the margins. It closes with Porphyry's wrap-up sentence (Düring 77.18), and there are about 24,000 characters of translation plus notes. Цыпин's own note cites the work as «псевдо-аристотелевский трактат „О слышимом“ (наст. изд., с. 81–86)». Since everything that survives of De audibilibus is what Porphyry quotes, this is a complete annotated Russian translation of the extant text.
(2) EXCERPTS: Е. В. Афонасин, «Теофраст о музыке», Дополнение 2, ΣΧΟΛΗ 6.1 (2012), pp. 125–133, with the De audibilibus excerpts on pp. 127–129 (https://cyberleninka.ru/article/n/teofrast-o-muzyke). This translates the opening (800a1–8) and phrases from 801a6–10 and 803a5–12 (plus a sentence after that). It was reprinted in Афонасин, Афонасина, Щетников, ΜΟΥΣΙΚΗ ΤΕΧΝΗ. Очерки истории античной музыки (СПб.: РХГА, 2013; 2nd ed. 2015). Its English abstract says the book has "extracts from the Peripatetic De audibilibus".
(3) Gaps in the bibliographies: Е. В. Орлов & О. С. Егорова, «Перечень русских переводов сочинений Аристотеля», Respublica Literaria 6.2 (2025) 71–101 (cyberleninka) lists only the Афонасин fragments and misses Цыпин 2013. The catalogue at aristoteles.philosophy.nsc.ru/node/68 says «Переводы: Не найдено», but it only covers works up to 1984.
PROBLEMATA XI (on voice): I found no Russian translation. Орлов–Егорова 2025 lists only Book XV (Щетников, ΣΧΟΛΗ 13.2, 2019), Book XIX (Щетников, ΣΧΟΛΗ 6.1, 2012, 87–97), Book XXX (Россиус, 2015) and Латышев's geographical fragments (1890/1947). Several cyberleninka API searches turned up nothing on Book XI. I could not check whether Лосев–Шестаков, «Античная музыкальная эстетика» (1960) has any XI excerpts, so that remains unknown.
Searches run: Google ("О слышимом" Аристотель перевод; Очерки истории античной музыки Порфирий; Порфирий «Комментарий к Гармонике» перевод; «О слышимом» Порфирий перевод полностью). Google then showed a CAPTCHA, which I did not attempt. I also ran about 15 cyberleninka API queries, checked the РУССКИЙ АРИСТОТЕЛЬ catalogue, and ran Bing queries (Цыпин Птолемей Гармоника Порфирий 2013; Античная музыкальная эстетика 1960).

There are several complete English translations.
(1) T. Loveday & E. S. Forster, "De audibilibus", in The Works of Aristotle Translated into English, vol. VI: Opuscula (Oxford: Clarendon, 1913). This is public domain: archive.org/details/workstranslatedi06arisuoft and en.wikisource.org "The Works of Aristotle – Vol. 6 – Opuscula (1913).djvu".

verification.recommendation: De audibilibus should be dropped as a Neoscholia candidate. It has a complete annotated Russian translation (Цыпин 2013, inside Porphyry's commentary) and full translations in English (Loveday–Forster 1913, Hett 1936, Barker 1989/2015), German (Klein 1972) and Italian (Raffa 2016). The only real gap is Problemata XI (on voice), which as far as I can find has never been translated into Russian. It is modest but well defined, but since it is already in English, German, French and Italian, it is a low-novelty filler and not a priority unit.

verification.en_found: CONFIRMED, with caveats. J. Raasted, The Hagiopolites: A Byzantine Treatise on Musical Theory, preliminary edition, CIMAGL 45 (Copenhagen 1983), pp. 1–99. It has the Greek text (normalised and diplomatic columns), a critical apparatus, an English translation, notes and an index. I checked the PDF and OCR directly. The 'TRANSLATION' sections cover §§1–55 (the whole Byzantine part), §§90–96 and §§100–105. Raasted says the translation was 'made en route' as a running commentary and is 'frequently… rather a paraphrase than a translation', especially at the beginning. Passages he did not understand are marked with question marks or given word for word. He deliberately left untranslated the paragraphs taken over from Anonymus III Bellermann (§§56–89, 98), which he calls 'absurd' and untranslatable as transmitted. §99 (an Alypian diatonic scale list) has no translation either. So the English is substantially complete for the treatise proper, but preliminary and in places a paraphrase. Other English: short quoted passages in Gertsman's Petersburg Theoretikon (1994, bilingual), and probably in specialist literature such as Troelsgård's Byzantine Neumes (not checked). Raasted's edition is freely downloadable (see source_text), so the English is easy to get.

It gives the Greek text and a French translation ('Traduction du Ier… Ve fragment') of §§90–97 and 100–105, i.e. the ancient-theory appendix. Raasted's introduction confirms this, and I checked the text on archive.org (item NoticesEtExtraitsDesMss16P2, Public Domain Mark). GREEK TEXT ONLY: J.-B. Thibaut, Monuments de la notation ekphonétique et hagiopolite de l'Église grecque (St Petersburg 1913), pp. 57–60, gives the Greek of §§1–27 (whether it also translates is unverified). Du Cange's Glossarium (1688) quotes passages. GERMAN: J. Tzetzes, Über die altgriechische Musik in der griechischen Kirche (München 1874), and C. Floros, Universale Neumenkunde (1970) use and quote the treatise. Whether either translates continuous passages is unverified. D. verification.source_text: The best usable text is Raasted 1983 (CIMAGL 45). It is free to read and download (open access, but copyrighted and not openly licensed) at https://cimagl.saxo.ku.dk/download/45/45Raasted1-99.pdf. A third-party copy with OCR is at https://archive.org/details/raasted-1983-the-hagiopolites (rights unclear). It is the only complete edition: there is a single manuscript (Paris. gr. 360, fols. 216–237), plus Sinait. gr. 1764 for §§56–96 and 98–99, and the Perne (1811) and Sypsomo (1856) copies. A final critical edition was planned for Corpus Scriptorum de Re Musica, and the 2025 Plainsong & Medieval Music citation suggests it has not yet appeared. PUBLIC-DOMAIN partial texts: Vincent 1847, Notices et extraits XVI/2, pp. 259–281 (§§90–97, 100–105; https://archive.org/details/NoticesEtExtraitsDesMss16P2, Public Domain Mark), and Thibaut 1913, pp. 57–60 (§§1–27). For §§56–89, use Najock's Teubner edition, Anonyma de musica scripta Bellermanniana (Leipzig 1975; copyrighted). Size is manageable: c. 105 short paragraphs, about 90 printed pages including apparatus. The Greek is often lacunose and corrupt, so an LLM translation will need close expert checking, especially in §§1–55.
verification.recommendation: It is a reasonable Neoscholia candidate for Russian: the first full Russian translation would be new, since Gertsman gives only scattered excerpts and calls the work «Святоградец». It is weak on the 'untranslated' criterion for English, because Raasted's English is freely online, although preliminary and partly paraphrase, and it is medieval rather than ancient. Start with §§1–55, the unique Byzantine chant-theory section, translated into Russian from Raasted's text checked against Thibaut. Alternatively, start with the ancient-material appendix §§90–105 (Pythagoras' hammers, inventions of aulos and syrinx, consonance theory), which has a public-domain Greek text in Vincent 1847.

Public domain:
- M. Gerbert, Scriptores ecclesiastici de musica sacra potissimum I (St. Blasien, 1784), pp. 125–152. It is based mainly on a Strasbourg manuscript later lost in a fire, which makes it an indirect witness to a complete copy.

- Mühlmann 1914 gives emendations to Gerbert from the manuscripts.

- ALIMUS (Gerbert)
- ALIMU (Migne)

It is a reasonable Russian-first project, since only one unpublished fragment by Ренёва exists, though it falls outside the antiquity priority. If pursued, start with the principal treatise's opening sections, the Boethian proportions and the eight tropi (Gerbert I, 125–128). For an English version, a new annotated translation of the full text could replace Heard's.

Шестаков (ред.), «Музыкальная эстетика западноевропейского средневековья и Возрождения» (М.: Музыка, 1966), the section «РЕГИНО ИЗ ПРЮМА (?—915 годы)» runs about pp. 189–194. It has a short intro by Шестаков and then «Об изучении гармонии», with the credit line «Перевод Н. Ревякиной». The source given is "Reginonis, De harmonica institutione, MPL t. 132, p. 491". The translation is about 1,350 Russian words. It covers the passages on musica naturalis vs artificialis, the music of the heavens, the ethical effects of music (Saul, Elisha), music in animals, and artificial music, ending with the 'musicus vs cantor' passage. That corresponds roughly to §§4–7 and §18 of the Migne/Gerbert numbering, with at least one cut marked <...>. The section is about 20% of a Latin text of roughly 7,000 words. Not translated: §§1–3 (the dedication, modal anomalies and the eight tones), §§8–17 (etymology, vox/sonus, Pythagorean consonances, intervals) and §19, plus the Tonarius. I checked it in the full text at yanko.lib.ru/books/music/mus-aeth--west-mid-r.htm (table of contents and body) and at early-music.narod.ru/biblioteka/estetika-mages-renais/estetika-mages-renais-15.htm. The anthology was reissued in a 2nd edition by Юрайт (urait.ru). The excerpt is still cited, e.g. М. Ю. Аркан, Tempus et Memoria 2010, which also points to an online repost at m-kultura.ru/2006/01/liki/gesse. I found no full or other Russian translation. pravenc.ru («Регинон Прюмский», Православная энциклопедия) lists only Стасюлевич's 1864 Russian fragments of the Chronicon, nothing for the Epistola. The ru.wikipedia entry «Регино Прюмский» lists Gerbert, Coussemaker and Fiori 2011, with no Russian version. Cyberleninka API searches for «Регино Прюмский», «Регинон Прюмский», «Регино из Прюма» and «Regino Prüm» found 0 translations. Bing/DDG searches for «Регино из Прюма» перевод, «Об изучении гармонии» Регино, "Epistola de harmonica institutione" Регино, and Регинон тонарий also found nothing beyond the 1966 excerpt.
verification.en_found: FULL (unpublished) English translation: Mary Protase LeRoux, "The 'De harmonica institutione' and 'Tonarius' of Regino of Prüm", PhD thesis, Catholic University of America, Washington DC, 1965 (c1967). It is in the series Studies in Music (CUA) no. 22, x+317 leaves (Google Books gives 634 pp.), and was distributed as a University Microfilms microfilm of the typescript, OCLC 1944603 / 23630764. The Brandeis catalogue record (search.library.brandeis.edu/discovery/fulldisplay/alma997982770101921/01BRAND_INST:BRAND) says: Latin text of the Epistola with English translation in parallel columns on leaves 22–84, and the Tonarius Latin/English on leaves 299–305. Google Books records: id=YApbvgAACAAJ and id=5zQ5AQAAIAAJ. Correction to the sweep: this is a CUA dissertation distributed on UMI microfilm, not a UPenn thesis, and it is complete, not partial. EXCERPTS: Weiss & Taruskin, Music in the Western World: A History in Documents (Schirmer 1984; 2nd ed. 2008), ch. 16 "The Emergence of Polyphony" includes a short Regino item (checked against the table of contents at dandelon.com). Scholarly articles quote and translate passages, e.g. C. Bower, "Natural and Artificial Music" (Musica Disciplina 1971) and S. Boynton, "The sources and significance of the Orpheus myth in Musica enchiriadis and Regino's Epistola", Early Music History 18 (1999) 47–74. I did not verify how much of Boynton's article is translated. NOT included: Strunk/Treitler, Source Readings (rev. 1998). I checked its full table of contents and the medieval theory section has only Musica enchiriadis, Alia musica, Pseudo-Odo, Guido and later authors. No published, peer-reviewed full English book translation exists.

verification.source_text: Public-domain editions: M. Gerbert, Scriptores ecclesiastici de musica sacra I (St. Blasien 1784; repr. Hildesheim 1963), pp. 230–247. This was reprinted in Migne, PL 132, cols. 483–502 (Tonarius not included; the Tonarius is in Coussemaker, Scriptores II (1867), pp. 1–73, a poor transcription). There is a digital Migne text, about 7,000 Latin words with a 19-item synopsis, at la.wikisource.org/wiki/De_harmonica_(Regino_Prumiensis), sourced from Corpus Corporum (mlat.uzh.ch). A Migne PDF is at documentacatholicaomnia.eu (04z/z_0882-0915__Regino_Prumiensis_Abbas__De_Harmonica_Institutione__MLT.pdf.html). The TML normally carries a Gerbert-based text, but its main site is currently in an outage with only a provisional service, so I did not check it. The modern critical edition is M. Bernhard, Clavis Gerberti I (München 1989), pp. 39–73. It is in copyright, and a translation should collate against it. Chartier's 1965 Ottawa thesis also has an established text, open to read but not openly licensed.
verification.recommendation: A weak candidate: complete translations exist in English (LeRoux 1965, an unpublished microfilm dissertation), Italian (Fiori 2011, published) and French (Chartier 1965, an open-access thesis), and there is a Russian excerpt of about 20% (Revyakina 1966). It is also a Carolingian text (c. 900), outside the antiquity-first priority. If it is pursued, aim for the first complete Russian translation (plus a new accessible English one), collated against Bernhard 1989. Start with §§1–3 (the dedication to Ratbod, modal anomalies and the eight tones), which have never been translated into Russian, then the technical §§8–17 on consonances, also missing from the Russian.

verification.source_text:
Best scholarly text: Wolfram and Hannick 1997 (CSRM 5), which is in copyright.

Best openly available text: L. Tardo, L'antica melurgia bizantina (1938), Greek text pp. 207–220 and the following pieces, from Lavra 1656. Scanned with OCR at https://archive.org/details/tardo-1938-lantica-melurgia-bizantina. Tardo died in 1967, so the book is probably still in copyright in the US until the end of 2033. Italian law protects critical editions for only 20 years, so the Greek text itself is probably free in Italy; check this before relying on it.

Public-domain partial texts: Thibaut, Revue de l'Orient Chrétien 6 (1901), pp. 593–609, and Rebours, ROC 9 (1904), pp. 299–309, and 10 (1905), pp. 1–14. I could not find these ROC volumes on archive.org; Gallica or HathiTrust may have them.

Gertsman 1994 (RAIK 63 Greek text with an apparatus) is in copyright. A third-party scan is on archive.org (Collection-of-Evgeny-Gertsman).
verification.recommendation: Not a good Neoscholia candidate as an "untranslated" text. Gertsman (Petersburg Theoreticon, 1994) already published the Greek text with both Russian and English translations and commentary (RAIK 63, fol. 41–51v, plus the opening from Tardo), and Wolfram and Hannick give a full German critical translation. The work is also late Byzantine to post-Byzantine, well outside the antiquity priority. Drop it, or keep it in reserve only for a new RU/EN version of the 1997 critical text: first compare the ten Wolfram–Hannick pieces with Gertsman's seven sections and translate only those he lacks.

name: Musical documents and music in non-theoretical genres (scores, hymns, inscriptions, papyri, lexica, scholia, organology)
overview:
Musical documents and non-theoretical musical texts form the largest gap in this area. The literary and encyclopaedic sources are largely available in Russian: Athenaeus complete (Golinkevich, 2003–2010), Lucian's De saltatione (Baranov, 1935), Libanius Or. 64 (Shestakov, 1914–16, reprinted 2014), Timotheus' Persae (Shestakov 1904; Gasparov) and Proclus' Chrestomathy (Garadja, 2022). The notated music has no complete Russian translation. Pöhlmann & West's Documents of Ancient Greek Music (2001; about 61 items) gives no translations even in English. In Russian only scattered pieces exist: Seikilos and a literal Limenios by Tsypin (2013, 2019), and Mesomedes' notated hymns in 1930s music anthologies. E. V. Gertsman has studied Pollux (1988 article; 2022 monograph), the ancient organ (2004) and instrument writings (2020). However, no continuous annotated Russian translation of these sources was found, so their status is "partial or unverified".

In English, coverage is scattered: West 1992, Landels 1999 and Furley–Bremer 2001 for the epigraphic paeans (collected on attalus.org), and Loeb Select Papyri. Pollux has had no modern translation, but CUP lists one for February 2027. Choricius' Apologia mimorum has none (French Pernet 2019, Czech Šípová). Hero's Pneumatica exists in English (Woodcroft 1851) but not in Russian.

The best Russian gaps are: the full notated-music corpus, Pollux IV on music and dance, Mesomedes, the epigraphic paeans, decrees for musicians, papyrus contracts for musicians, Hero's sound devices, Choricius, and the Mesopotamian tuning tablets.
already_translated_ru:
Complete in Russian (verified): Athenaeus, Deipnosophists, including Book XIV (Н. Т. Голинкевич, Наука 2003/2010); Lucian, «О пляске» (Н. П. Баранов, 1935); Libanius Or. 64, «К Аристиду за плясунов» (С. П. Шестаков, 1914–16, reprinted Квадривиум 2014); Timotheus, «Персы» (Д. П. Шестаков 1904; М. Л. Гаспаров); Proclus, Chrestomathy, Phot. Bibl. 239 (А. В. Гараджа, 2022). Single musical documents: Seikilos and Limenios (В. Г. Цыпин, 2013 and 2019).

Theory, for reference: Tsypin, ed., «Музыкальные писатели античной Греции» (2019). It contains Ps.-Plutarch, Cleonides, Alypius, Bacchius, Gaudentius, Nicomachus, Theon, the Sectio canonis and the Anonymi Bellermann. Also in Russian: Ptolemy with Porphyry (Цыпин 2013), Aristoxenus (Цыпин 1997), Boethius (С. Н. Лебедев 2012/2019) and Problemata XIX (ΣΧΟΛΗ 2012). Vitruvius X.8 is in Russian (Петровский 1936; this specific claim not re-verified).

verification.title: Documents of Ancient Greek Music: the corpus of notated songs and instrumental pieces (Pöhlmann–West, DAGM). Proposed first unit: the Delphic paeans of Athenaios and Limenios
verification.ru_found:
No complete Russian translation of the corpus exists, but more of it is already translated than the sweep reported. Most importantly, the proposed first unit is half done.
(1) LIMENIOS, paean and prosodion (FD III 2.138), already fully translated. V. G. Tsypin, «Античный квантитативный лад», Научный вестник Московской консерватории 10/4 (39), Dec 2019, pp. 8–43, DOI 10.26176/mosconsv.2019.39.4.001. Open PDF: https://nv.mosconsv.ru/sites/default/files/2020-10/19_4_08-43_tsypin_0.pdf. I extracted the text: it gives a complete Russian prose translation of all eight sections, I–VII (the paean) and VIII (the prosodion), with lacunae marked. It opens «Придите к сей издали видной, пригодной для хороводов парнасской двуглавой…». The author says the translation is only for general information and does not reproduce the metre. It sits beside his transcription and modal analysis.
(2) MESOMEDES, Hymn to Nemesis and Hymn to the Sun (both notated DAGM pieces). Translated into Russian verse by М. Е. Грабарь-Пассек in «Памятники поздней античной поэзии и прозы II–V века» (М.: Наука, 1964), pp. 29–33. I checked this in the djvu text on archive.org (item pamyatniki-pozdney-antichnoy-poezii-i-prozy-ii-v-veka-1964), and the table of contents reads «Месомед. Пер. М. Е. Грабарь-Пассек». The same section also has Mesomedes' non-notated poems. The Hymn to the Muse/Calliope is NOT in this book. The sweep missed this source: it named only the 1933 music anthologies. It is cited as the Russian Nemesis translation by O. G. Шадский (2023, cyberleninka).
(3) SEIKILOS: Tsypin's translation in Птолемей, Гармоника; Порфирий, Комментарий (М.: МГК, 2013), pp. 399–404, quoted in ru.wikipedia «Эпитафия Сейкила». There are also many popular versions.
(4) 1933: Иванов-Борецкий, «Музыкально-историческая хрестоматия», вып. 1, and Э. К. Розенов, «Музыкальные памятники Эллады» (Музгиз). Both are cited in ru.wikipedia's Mesomedes article. Rozenov's book is a set of musical restorations, not a philological translation. I could not see the contents of either.
(5) Euripides' Orestes 338–344 and Iphigenia in Aulis 784–792 (the notated papyri) are covered by the complete Russian translations of those plays.
NOT FOUND: any Russian translation of the ATHENAIOS paean (FD III 2.137), the Oxyrhynchus Christian hymn, or the many small papyrus fragments. Also unverified: whether Tsypin's anthology «Музыкальные писатели античной Греции» (Памятники музыкальной науки IV, М.: МГК, 2019, 536 pp.) contains any notated documents, such as the Anonymi Bellermann exercises.
Searches: the WebSearch quota was used up, so I ran more than 25 Russian queries through the CyberLeninka API (Лимений/Лимения, Дельфийский гимн, Дельфийские пеаны, Месомед/Мезомед, Сейкил, Гимн Немесиде, Оксиринхский гимн, пеан Аполлону нотация, Документы древнегреческой музыки, Цыпин). I also searched Russian Wikipedia, the Научный вестник МГК archive (Tsypin's five articles there), archive.org/Open Library full text, and Афонасин's bibliography «Античная музыка» (ΣΧΟΛΗ 2012), which lists no Russian translation of DAGM.
verification.en_found:
There is no translated corpus. The BMCR review 2003.04.08 (W. Johnson) says DAGM gives, for each of its 61 items, the Greek text, notation, apparatus, a transcription and a brief technical commentary. It mentions no translations. However, the main pieces, including the proposed first unit, exist in full English versions.
- Delphic paeans: J. G. Landels, Music in Ancient Greece and Rome (Routledge 1999), pp. 231 and 237 (per en.wikipedia "Delphic Hymns"), translates both. https://www.attalus.org/poetry/paeans.html gives both Athenaeus and Limenius complete with lacunae marked, "adapted from the translation by J.G. Landels", with the Greek from PHI FD III 2.137 and 2.138.
- Brown and d'Angour 2017 translate part of Athenaios.
- Furley & Bremer, Greek Hymns I–II (Tübingen 2001), vol. I translations and vol. II text and commentary. BMCR 2002.05.36 mentions recordings of "two paians to Apollo" with notation, so the Delphic chapter very probably includes both. I recall them as nos. 2.6–2.7, but did not verify the numbers.
- Mesomedes' hymns: Landels 1999 (Hymn to the Sun, Prayer to Calliope and Apollo); Cosgrove 2011 (An Ancient Christian Hymn with Musical Notation, pp. 69–70).
- Seikilos and the Oxyrhynchus hymn: countless versions (West 1992; Landels; Cosgrove 2011 for P.Oxy. 1786). West, Ancient Greek Music (1992), ch. 10, and Mathiesen, Apollo's Lyre (1999), discuss the documents, with at least partial translations.
- Euripides fragments: covered by every translation of Orestes and IA.

The public-domain base is K. von Jan, Musici Scriptores Graeci, Supplementum: Melodiarum reliquiae (Teubner 1899). It is on archive.org as musiciscriptores02jank (v.2, 72 pp.; the sweep's URL is correct) and as musiciscriptores00jank and musiciscriptoresjanksupp. I confirmed the text: it covers both Delphic hymns, Seikilos, Mesomedes and others. Jan 1895, Musici Scriptores Graeci, also has the 1895 versions of the melodies (archive.org musiciscriptores01jank). Jan is badly outdated for the Delphic paeans, which were rearranged after 1899, and it lacks all the post-1899 papyri.
For the Delphic paeans, the free readable texts are PHI Greek Inscriptions FD III 2.137 (https://epigraphy.packhum.org/text/239433) and FD III 2.138 (https://epigraphy.packhum.org/text/239435). These are free to read but not openly licensed. Fouilles de Delphes III.2 (Colin 1909–13) may be public domain, but I did not check whether it is online.
For papyri: papyri.info (DDbDP, CC BY) has the texts, though it encodes the musical notation only partly.
The authoritative modern edition remains Pöhlmann & West, DAGM (OUP 2001), which is in copyright.
verification.recommendation: The corpus as a whole is a reasonable candidate: it has never been translated and annotated as one body in any language, and an AI-assisted bilingual edition (text, translation, notation commentary) would be new. But the proposed first unit is weak. Limenios already has a full Russian prose translation (Tsypin 2019, open access) and full English ones (Landels; attalus.org; probably Furley–Bremer), and Mesomedes' Nemesis and Helios hymns are in Russian (Grabar-Passek 1964). Start instead with the Athenaios paean, for which I found no Russian translation, as a Russian-first unit, or better with a batch of the untranslated papyrus fragments (e.g. the Oslo, Michigan and Berlin papyri) whose texts are on papyri.info.

Best source: E. Bethe, Pollucis Onomasticon, fasc. 1 (Books I–V), Lexicographi Graeci IX.1 (Leipzig: Teubner, 1900). Public domain. Scan at https://archive.org/details/pollucisonomasti01polluoft. Its OCR text (djvu.txt) is garbled, with Greek read as Latin letters, so it needs fresh polytonic OCR.

The Perseus catalog entry tlg0542.tlg001.opp-grc1 only links to the Bethe scans. The First1KGreek file tlg0542.tlg001.1st1K-grc1 (CC BY-SA 4.0) contains only Hultsch's 1864 metrological excerpts, so there is no open TEI text of Book IV. Size of the unit: about 56 Bethe sections, roughly 8–10 Teubner pages, which is easy to handle.
verification.recommendation: A good candidate for Russian: there is no continuous Russian translation, only Gertsman's scattered quotations, but check his 2022 Kvadrivium monograph first. The English value is limited: CUP's complete translation is due February 2027, Csapo and Slater already translate IV.99–112 in abridged form, and Barker translates IV.84. Start with the purely musical block IV.57–90 (song genres, string instruments, kitharodic nomos, auloi, auletic nomoi including the Pythikos nomos, salpinx), with music-focused commentary, and drop or postpone 99–112.

Best first unit: a complete, annotated, philologically exact Russian Mesomedes, starting with the never-translated pieces (Isis, Sponge, short Horologion, Swan, Gnat) and the notated Muse/Calliope prooimia with notation commentary. Powell's edition is not freely online. J. U. Powell, Collectanea Alexandrina (Oxford, 1925) has Philodamus, Aristonous, Isyllus, Makedonikos and the Erythraean paean. The 1925 printing should be public domain in the US, but archive.org has only the 1970 reprint, and only for loan (collectaneaalexa0000unse, access-restricted). HathiTrust could not be checked because it returned 403. This corrects the sweep's "public domain, archive.org".
Freely readable alternatives:
- Philodamus: Weil, BCH 19 (1895) 393ff, on Persée (free).
- All five inscriptions: PHI Greek Inscriptions (free to read, but not openly licensed): BCH 19 (1895) 393 for Philodamus; FD III 2.191 / Syll.³ 449 for Aristonoos; IG IV²,1 128 for Isyllus; Erythrai 1 (IK Erythrai 205), lines 56–76, for the Erythraean paean; IG II² 4473 + SEG 23.126 for Makedonikos.

The modern critical editions, Furley and Bremer vol. II (2001) and Käppel (1992), are under copyright.
verification.recommendation: This is a poor Neoscholia candidate as a group. Five of the six texts were published in Russian in 1999 (Голубец and Ярхо, «Эллинские поэты», Ладомир) and are online at ancientrome.ru, and all six exist in English (Furley and Bremer 2001, among others). The texts are cult poetry with no musical notation or theory, so their value for music research is limited. The only real gap is Makedonikos' paean (IG II² 4473; about 20 lines, no Russian translation found). That would at most be a small unit, perhaps paired with a scholarly Russian translation of the parts of the Isyllus inscription Голубец left out (sections A–C and E).

verification.source_text: Best open source: the Greek texts in the Duke Databank of Documentary Papyri (papyri.info, DDbDP and HGV, often with HGV translations). It is licensed CC BY 3.0; I confirmed the license in the idp.data README, https://github.com/papyri/idp.data. The papyri.info website currently sits behind an Anubis bot check, but the XML data is downloadable from GitHub. For choosing documents, Tedeschi 2011 is the best checklist, with updated readings and apparatus. It is free to read on OpenstarTs but copyrighted, so use it as a finding aid and cross-check, not as a base text. The early editions are public domain and on archive.org: Grenfell–Hunt, P.Oxy. I (1898), III (1903), VII (1910), X (1914); P.Hib. I (1906); Wilcken, Chrestomathie (1912). Later editions such as P.Oxy. XXXIV (1968), LXXIV (2009) and P.Heid. IV are in copyright, but their Greek texts are available on papyri.info under CC BY.
verification.recommendation: This is a moderate candidate at best. Russian is still open (no translation found), but the corpus is not untranslated in modern languages: Tedeschi 2011 already gives all 80 documents in Greek with full Italian translations, and the main contracts have English translations (Hunt–Edgar, the P.Oxy. volumes, Westermann, Rowlandson). It is also social history of music rather than music theory. If pursued, start with a first Russian translation, with a collected English version, of the 23 contracts of engagement in Tedeschi's Appendix I, taken from papyri.info (CC BY 3.0). A good pilot is the Oxyrhynchite symphonia contracts (P.Oxy. X 1275, XXXIV 2721, LXXIV 5014–5016) plus P.Corn. 9 and SB I 5810. Give priority to the contracts with no English translation (C.P.R. XVIII 1, P.Strasb. V 341, BGU VII 1648, P.Heid. IV 328, P.Med. I 47).

verification.ru_found:
I found no Russian translation, full or partial, of any document in this group. That covers the Kleochares decree (SIG 450), the Polygnota decree (SIG 738), the decree for the hydraulis player Antipatros (SIG 737), the Soteria lists (SIG 424, 489, 509, 690) and the Amphictyonic and Delphic decrees for the Athenian technitai (SIG 399, 692, 698, 704). What exists in Russian is paraphrase or a few quoted words:
(1) E. V. Bulycheva, "Дипломатическая деятельность технитов Диониса в Афинах (II–I вв. до н.э.)", Метаморфозы истории, 2018 (https://cyberleninka.ru/article/n/diplomaticheskaya-deyatelnost-tehnitov-dionisa-v-afinah-ii-i-vv-do-n-e). It cites Syll.³ 399 and paraphrases the privileges, but gives no translated text.
(2) The Russian Wikipedia article "Гидравлос" (mirror: https://dic.academic.ru/dic.nsf/ruwiki/1776310) quotes about three words from the Antipatros decree, garbled and without a source. This is not a translation.
(3) M. V. Skrzhinskaya, «Древнегреческие праздники в Элладе и Северном Причерноморье». I checked chapters VI and XI on history.niv.ru and found no translated Delphic inscriptions. One snippet suggests she discusses the Soteria lists (a Bosporan chorus trainer) in paraphrase; I could not open that chapter (sno.pro1.ru failed with an SSL error).
Searches run (8 in Russian): Дельфы почётный декрет кифаред/Сотерии; Дионисийские техниты Дельфы ВДИ; "дионисийских технитов" декрет амфиктионов перевод; Полигнота фиванская арфистка; гидравлос Антипатр Элевтерна; техниты Дионис надписи cyberleninka; Булычева техниты диссертация; Сотерии списки участников. I did not check Лосев–Шестаков «Античная музыкальная эстетика» (1960) directly. From memory it contains literary texts only, not inscriptions, but treat that as unconfirmed. I also did not check the Soviet source readers (хрестоматии), the ВДИ archive, or elibrary.
verification.en_found:
English is "partial" in the sense that not every decree is translated, but the core documents are much better covered than the sweep suggested. Checked directly this session:
(a) attalus.org, SIG translation index (https://www.attalus.org/docs/sig.html). It gives complete, unattributed English translations, with links to the PHI Greek text, of:
- Soteria lists: SIG 424 (all categories: rhapsodes, kitharists, kitharodes, choreutai, auletes, tragic and comic troupes), 489, 509, 690
- technitai documents: SIG 399, 460, 692, 698 (the 128/7 Pythaïs decree naming Limenios and Athenaios), 704, 705
- honorary decrees: SIG 450 Kleochares, 689 (a harpist from Pergamon), 699 (epic poets of Athens), 737 Antipatros of Eleutherna the hydraulis player (complete), 738 Polygnota of Thebes and her cousin Lykinos (complete), 739, 740
- Pythaïs lists: SIG 697, 711, 728.
(b) Attic Inscriptions Online (atticinscriptions.com) has an FD III 2 series in English. Examples: FD III 2, 137 and 138 (the Athenaios and Limenios hymns with their headings; translated by T. Hirsch and C. Albert); FD III 2, 140 (an Athenian decree on the Soteria; translated by C. Huayna Avila); FD III 2, 66. It also has pages under Le Guen 2001 numbering (e.g. "Le Guen TE 15", "Le Guen 84-88"), so more technitai documents are probably translated there; those pages returned server errors.
(c) The Poeti vaganti database (CHS Harvard and Sapienza; https://poetivaganti.chs.harvard.edu/) gives Greek and English with commentary, e.g. FD III 2, 78 (Kleochares).
In print, not verified this session: Csapo & Slater, The Context of Ancient Drama (1995), which probably translates the Soteria lists and the Amphictyonic decrees for the technitai; Furley & Bremer, Greek Hymns (2001), which attalus cites for Aristonoos; Pöhlmann & West 2001, nos. 20–21 (hymns). Barker's Greek Musical Writings does not cover inscriptions. Still largely untranslated: the many shorter FD III proxeny and honorary decrees for individual kitharodes, auletes and poets that are not in SIG.
Only 2 English searches ran before the search budget ran out (Kleochares/SIG 450; Antipatros hydraulis). The rest was checked by fetching attalus.org, AIO and CHS pages directly.
verification.other_found: French: B. Le Guen, Les associations de technites dionysiaques à l'époque hellénistique (2001), a corpus with French translations (per the sweep; AIO uses its numbering). Also, unverified this session: A. Bélis, Corpus des inscriptions de Delphes III, Les hymnes à Apollon (1992); G. Nachtergael, Les Galates en Grèce et les Sôtéria de Delphes (1977), an edition of the Soteria lists. German: S. Aneziri, Die Vereine der dionysischen Techniten (2003), per the sweep; I did not confirm whether it translates the documents in full. Italian: the Poeti vaganti database has Italian commentary. M. Guarducci, "Poeti vaganti e conferenzieri dell'età ellenistica" (1929) is an edition and study, not verified as a translation. A. Cinalli has an article on Antipatros in the CHS Research Bulletin (linked from attalus SIG 737). I found no Spanish translation; not searched.
verification.source_text: The best public-domain source is W. Dittenberger, Sylloge Inscriptionum Graecarum, 3rd ed. (1915–1924), which covers all the core documents listed above. It is out of copyright and scans are widely available, e.g. archive.org; no specific URL was confirmed this session. The early Fouilles de Delphes III fascicles (G. Colin, FD III 2, 1909–1913; É. Bourguet, FD III 1) are probably public domain. FD III 3 (Daux and Salaç, 1932–1943) and Le Guen 2001 are still in copyright. Greek texts are free to read but not openly licensed on PHI Greek Inscriptions (https://epigraphy.packhum.org; attalus links each SIG text there, e.g. FD 3.3.249–250 for Polygnota). The Poeti vaganti database also gives Greek texts. The size is manageable: the core group is about 20 documents, mostly short. The Soteria lists are prosopographical catalogues that are easy for an LLM but need careful notes.
verification.recommendation: This is a moderate candidate, with value mainly in Russian. In English the core documents are already freely available (attalus.org, AIO, Poeti vaganti), so new English adds little except commentary on the music. Start with a Russian-first annotated set of the core decrees and lists (SIG 737, 738, 450, 424, 698 or 399, 689), and treat as genuinely new the FD III honorary decrees for kitharodes, auletes and poets that are absent from SIG and attalus.

No Russian translation of the Pneumatica, full or partial, turned up anywhere. The organ chapters are the open question.

Searches (7 in Russian), all without result: «Герон Александрийский Пневматика перевод на русский»; «Герон водяной орган гидравлос перевод текста Герцман»; «Герцман "Античный орган"»; «"Пневматика" Герона перевод с греческого "водяной орган" фрагмент»; «Герон "Пневматика" русский перевод издание хрестоматия»; «Пневматика … ΣΧΟΛΗ / ВДИ / Аристей»; «"Пневматика" "пер. с греч"».

Sources checked directly, with no Heron translation in any of them:
- The «Античные писатели» dictionary entry on ancientrome.ru lists no Russian translation.
- The ru.wikipedia articles «Герон» and «Гидравлос» list none. For the organ, «Гидравлос» cites only Vitruvius X.8 in Petrovsky's translation (1936).
- Лосев–Шестаков, «Античная музыкальная эстетика» (1960): full text searched. No Heron and no hydraulis passage; the only hit is the word «гидравлисты» in a list of modes from another author.
- Герцман, «Музыка Древней Греции и Рима» (1995) and «Античное музыкальное мышление» (1986): full texts searched. No Heron.

Unresolved leads:
(a) Е. В. Герцман, «Античный орган» (СПб., 2004). Its existence is confirmed by the bibliography in the Православная энциклопедия article on Герцман (pravenc.ru/text/164903.html). Its contents could not be checked, and the subtitle and 62-page count given by the sweep remain unconfirmed. It may well contain a Russian version of Pneum. I.42 and should be checked in a library.
(b) Г. Дильс, «Античная техника» (М.–Л., 1934), the Russian translation of Diels' "Antike Technik". It may quote some Pneumatica automata in translation. Not checked.

The sweep's "partial" status therefore rests on an unverified guess. "Unknown" is the honest label: the work as a whole is untranslated into Russian, and whether I.42 has been translated hinges on the Gertsman 2004 brochure.
verification.en_found:
A complete English translation exists and is public domain: The Pneumatics of Hero of Alexandria, from the original Greek, London: Taylor, Walton and Maberly, 1851. Bennet Woodcroft edited it; Project Gutenberg #77400 (released 4 Dec 2025) credits Joseph George Greenwood as translator.

I downloaded the Gutenberg text (gutenberg.org/ebooks/77400). It covers all 78 sections, including the organs as §76 "An Altar Organ blown by manual Labour" and §77 "An Altar Organ blown by the agency of a Wind-mill". It also has the sounding automata: §14 a bird made to whistle, §15 birds that sing and fall silent by turns, §16 trumpets sounded by flowing water, §17 sounds on the opening of a temple door, §48 a whistling thyrsus, §49 an automaton blowing a trumpet, §68 a revolving singing bird, §75 a blackbird or Triton horn driven by a boiler.

There is also a modern English translation of I.42: Jean Perrot, The Organ from its Invention in the Hellenistic Period to the End of the Thirteenth Century, trans. Norma Deane, Oxford UP 1971 (French original 1965). Its chapter on the hydraulic organ contains a full annotated English translation of I.42 ("Construction of a Hydraulic Organ … Let ABΓΔ be a small 'altar' made of bronze"). An appendix (p. 295) prints the Greek of I.42 and Vitruvius X.8. Perrot only paraphrases I.43. Source: full text at archive.org/details/perrot-1972-the-organ-from-its-invention-in-the-hellenistic-period-to-the-end-of. Perrot also reports that W. Chappell (19th c.) translated Hero's organ passage.

Not in the standard music anthologies:
- Mathiesen, Apollo's Lyre (1999), pp. 226–29: paraphrases I.42 only, no translation.

It is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0: verbatim non-commercial reuse with attribution is allowed. Free PDF from https://www.peterlang.com/document/1068788 (free_download link), mirrored at archive.org/details/oapen-20.500.12657-41495; the OAPEN handle 20.500.12657/41495 sits behind a bot-check. The public-domain editio princeps is C. Graux, "Chorikios, Apologie des mimes", Revue de philologie 1 (1877), pp. 209–247, reprinted in Œuvres de Charles Graux II: Textes grecs (1886), pp. 39–77. It is full-view on archive.org at archive.org/details/lestextesgrecsau00grauuoft (marked NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT; the Greek OCR is usable but needs cleanup). The standard edition is Foerster–Richtsteig, Choricii Gazaei opera (Teubner 1929), pp. 344–380. Published in 1929, it should be public domain in the US since 2025, but I found no open scan: archive.org has only the restricted 1972 reprint, and I could not check HathiTrust (Cloudflare). Size: about 160 §§ and roughly 7,500–8,000 Greek words; it is Choricius' longest speech and manageable for an LLM workflow.
verification.recommendation: Still a viable candidate, since no English translation and no complete Russian one exist. But it is not "RU none": Фрейберг 1968 translated about 15% (sections I, V, VI, XX). It is also only marginally a music text: it concerns mime theatre, with music limited to mime songs and voice (§§130–141), the symposium aulos anecdote (§§152–154) and the closing Dionysus material. If chosen, start with Pernet §§130–154 on mime songs (ᾄσματα), euphony and the aulos, which are untranslated in both Russian and English, using Pernet's text checked against Graux 1877.

verification.en_found:
This refutes the claim that EN is "partial". Every tablet in the group has a complete English edition (transliteration plus translation), and there are two English collections.
- UET VII 74 (U.7/80, the main Ur tuning text): Gurney, "An Old Babylonian Treatise on the Tuning of the Harp", Iraq 30 (1968) 229–233, with autograph, transcription and translation. Revised in Gurney, "Babylonian Music Again", Iraq 56 (1994) 101–106. Wulstan, Iraq 30 (1968) 215–228.
- UET VI/3 899 (a duplicate of the same tuning text): Mirelman & Krispijn, Iraq 71 (2009) 43–52 (DOI 10.1017/S0021088900000735; paywalled, with a SOAS repository copy). Mirelman 2013 (AAWM 2.2, open access) says a complete translation of the tuning text is in Mirelman 2010, Archiv für Musikwissenschaft 67: 45–51.
- CBS 10996: Kilmer 1960, Orientalia 29 (transcription, translation, photo). Revised in Kilmer 1971, PAPS 115, and in West, Music & Letters 75 (1994) 161–179.
- UET VII 126 (U.3011), a source of Nabnitu XXXII, so the two candidate items overlap: Kilmer 1965, "The Strings of Musical Instruments…", in AS 16 (transcription and translation). Gurney's autograph is UET VII (1974) no. 126. The Nippur duplicate N 4782 is in Shaffer, Iraq 43 (1981).
- h.6: Duchesne-Guillemin, A Hurrian Musical Score from Ugarit (Undena 1984, monograph); Güterbock, RA 64 (1970); Kilmer, RA 68 (1974); Krispijn 2000/2001 (English translation of the lyrics, explicitly provisional); West 1994. The Hurrian lyrics are understood only provisionally.
- Collections: Dumbrill, The Archaeomusicology of the Ancient Near East (Trafford 2005) covers the whole corpus, and a PDF is on archive.org/details/richard-dumbrill-work-archive. Bayer, "The Mesopotamian Theory of Music and the Ugarit Notation – A Reexamination", and Kilmer, "Mesopotamian Music Theory Since 1977", both in Yuval 8 / Music in Antiquity (De Gruyter/Magnes 2014), give transliterations and translations of the String List, the Key-Number Table (CBS 10996) and the Tuning Text.

If pursued, make it a Russian-only annotated corpus, starting with the composite Ur tuning text (UET VII 74 plus its duplicate UET VI/3 899, about 30 lines), then the Nabnitu XXXII string and mode list. Put h.6 last, because its Hurrian lyrics can be translated only provisionally.
